notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0003] Use BillingError with snake_case codes: Raise `ledgerly.errors.BillingError(code, detail)` with snake_case codes such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`; match the existing `invalid_state` message format `f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0006] Record audit entry for every money movement: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", payment_id=... or invoice_id=..., amount=...). Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver (FIN-2026-03): accept keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Normalize money inputs with round_money before storing: Always pass monetary values through `ledgerly.money.round_money` before storing them on models or comparing against `ZERO`; never store raw input Decimals.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 0 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: a recent task that relied on this note failed a related review check.
- [at-0004] Reject bools when validating integer arguments: When validating an integer parameter, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)`) because `True`/`False` are ints in Python.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 1x, 1 passed, 0 failed)

item.title: Money is Decimal end-to-end, never float
item.content: In ledgerly, amounts must stay Decimal end-to-end with exactly two decimal places; convert inputs with `to_money`/`round_money` from `ledgerly.money` and never use float arithmetic. Convert rates or other numerics via `Decimal(str(x))` before multiplying a Decimal.
